## PASS 1 - BLIND HUNTER (the diff, and nothing else)

You get the diff at `specs/stories/code-review/issue-1153-eqc2-diff.txt` and **nothing else**. No
spec, no story file, no project context. Do not explore the repository. Do not go looking for the
spec. Read other files only to resolve an import path the diff itself leaves ambiguous.

### What this diff claims to be

A new pure predicate `isEquipmentOnMe(item)` in `equipment-derivation.js` (true for
`state` in `{carried, worn, active}`, false otherwise/for a null item), used to (a) REPLACE four
previously-duplicated inline `item.state === 'carried' || ... === 'worn' || ... === 'active'` checks
in `roll.js` and `roll-v2.js` (two call sites each) with calls to the shared function, and (b) drive a
new "On you" / "Stored elsewhere" text label added to six sections of `editor/sheet.js`'s equipment
renderer (Weapons, Armour, Other Combat Gear, Skill Gear, Tools/Utility, Narrative), computed as
`item.state === 'lost' ? null : (isEquipmentOnMe(item) ? 'On you' : 'Stored elsewhere')`. The
`Container` section is claimed to be deliberately EXCLUDED from the new label. Two test files are
updated: new behavioural tests for `isEquipmentOnMe` itself, and updated source-string checks for the
consolidated roll.js predicates.

**That is the shape it claims. Do not trust the shape - verify it.**

### What to hunt for

1. **The consolidation in `roll.js`/`roll-v2.js` is the highest-risk part of this diff** - it replaces
   INLINE, already-shipped logic with a function call. Compare the OLD inline condition
   (`item.state === 'carried' || item.state === 'worn' || item.state === 'active'`) against
   `isEquipmentOnMe`'s own body EXACTLY, character for character. Any divergence (a missing state, an
   extra state, a typo) silently changes which items grant a weapon-reference entry or a skill-bonus
   chip for every character in the game.
2. **The `locationLabel` helper's `lost` special-case**: `item.state === 'lost' ? null : ...` - trace
   every one of the six call sites in `sheet.js` to confirm a `null` return is actually handled
   correctly at each one (some sites build an array and `.filter(Boolean)` it; at least one site
   builds a joined string with `.filter(Boolean).join(' · ')`; the Narrative section handles it via a
   separate `loc` variable with its own conditional block) - a `null` slipping through unfiltered at
   any ONE of the six sites would render the literal string "null" in a player-facing sheet.
3. **Trivially-satisfiable assertions**: scan the new test assertions for anything that would pass even
   if the underlying logic were wrong.
4. **Self-contradiction within the diff**: does the AC/comment claim about Container exclusion actually
   hold - is there truly no `locationLabel` call anywhere in the Container-bucket render block, or did
   one slip in?
5. **Dead code**: is `isEquipmentOnMe` actually called from every site the diff's comments claim, or
   does any comment describe a consolidation that the code doesn't actually perform (e.g. a comment
   saying "consolidated onto isEquipmentOnMe" above a line that still has the old inline check)?
6. **Unused imports**: do `roll.js`/`roll-v2.js` still import `isEquipmentOnMe` if literally nothing in
   the final diff calls it, or vice versa (called but not imported, which would be a runtime
   ReferenceError)?

**STOP. Write your Pass 1 findings to
`specs/stories/code-review/issue-1153-eqc2-codex-findings.md` now, before reading further.**

+ * armourDefencePenalty above) - a carried-but-unworn breastplate is on you
+ * but grants no AR. This predicate answers "is it near me right now", not
+ * "is every possible bonus from it firing" - callers that need the latter

+ *

+ * kind of check per-consumer is the mistake to avoid.
+ *
+ * @param {object} item - a character's equipment[] entry (has `state`)
+ * @returns {boolean}
+ */
+export function isEquipmentOnMe(item) {
+  if (!item) return false;
+  return item.state === 'carried' || item.state === 'worn' || item.state === 'active';

// ── SPECIALTY TOGGLE ──
//
// Click handler for the specialty badges under the effective-pool line.
// Toggling a badge on adds its dice bonus to MOD; toggling off subtracts
// the same amount. The per-spec bonus is stored in state.specBonuses so
// we can reverse the exact amount even if the displayed bonus would be
// different at toggle-off time (e.g. character data changed mid-roll).

export function togSpec(badge) {
  if (!badge) return;
  const name = badge.dataset.spec;
  const bonus = parseInt(badge.dataset.bonus, 10) || 0;
  if (!name || !bonus) return;
  const existing = state.specBonuses[name];
  if (existing !== undefined) {
    state.MOD = state.MOD - existing;
    delete state.specBonuses[name];
  } else {
    state.MOD = state.MOD + bonus;
    state.specBonuses[name] = bonus;
  }
  updPool();
}

// ── EQUIPMENT CHIP TOGGLE (EQ-3) ──

export function togEquipChip(badge) {
  if (!badge) return;
  const id = badge.dataset.equip;
  const bonus = parseInt(badge.dataset.bonus, 10) || 0;
  if (!id || !bonus) return;

  if (state.activeEquipBonus && state.activeEquipBonus.catalogueId === id) {
    state.MOD -= state.activeEquipBonus.bonus;
    state.activeEquipBonus = null;
  } else {
    if (state.activeEquipBonus) {
      state.MOD -= state.activeEquipBonus.bonus;
    }
    state.MOD += bonus;
    state.activeEquipBonus = { catalogueId: id, bonus };
  }
  updPool();
}

      }).join('') + '</div>';
    }
  }

  el.innerHTML = html;
  updWeaponRef();
}

// ── SPECIALTY TOGGLE ──
//
// Click handler for the specialty badges under the effective-pool line.
// Toggling a badge on adds its dice bonus to MOD; toggling off subtracts
// the same amount. The per-spec bonus is stored in state.specBonuses so
// we can reverse the exact amount even if the displayed bonus would be
// different at toggle-off time (e.g. character data changed mid-roll).

export function togSpec(badge) {
  if (!badge) return;
  const name = badge.dataset.spec;
  const bonus = parseInt(badge.dataset.bonus, 10) || 0;
  if (!name || !bonus) return;
  const existing = state.specBonuses[name];
  if (existing !== undefined) {
    state.MOD = state.MOD - existing;
    delete state.specBonuses[name];
  } else {
    state.MOD = state.MOD + bonus;
    state.specBonuses[name] = bonus;
  }
  updPool();
}

// ── EQUIPMENT CHIP TOGGLE (EQ-3) ──

export function togEquipChip(badge) {
  if (!badge) return;
  const id = badge.dataset.equip;
  const bonus = parseInt(badge.dataset.bonus, 10) || 0;
  if (!id || !bonus) return;

  if (state.activeEquipBonus && state.activeEquipBonus.catalogueId === id) {
    state.MOD -= state.activeEquipBonus.bonus;
    state.activeEquipBonus = null;
  } else {
    if (state.activeEquipBonus) {
      state.MOD -= state.activeEquipBonus.bonus;
    }
    state.MOD += bonus;
    state.activeEquipBonus = { catalogueId: id, bonus };
  }
  updPool();
}

/**
 * equipment-derivation.js — armour penalty + derived-defence materialisation.
 *
 * Issue #879 (ADR-006). Lifts EQ-1's "calcDefence does not read the equipment
 * array without an ADR" gate. ADR-006 specifies:
 *
 *   D1: armourDefencePenalty(c, catalogueLookup?) reads c.equipment[] filtered
 *       by state === 'worn' + bucket === 'combat_gear' with isCombatGearArmourShaped(entry);
 *       injectable catalogue lookup (default: the ECM-5 cache reader).
 *
 *       EQC-1 (issue #1152, epic #1038, 2026-08-13): the old `armour` bucket
 *       merged into `combat_gear` (which also covers weapons). "Armour-shaped"
 *       is identified by `isCombatGearArmourShaped` (armour_value OR
 *       defence_penalty populated - see that function's own comment for why
 *       a single-field check was wrong) rather than by bucket alone — the
 *       epic's own "distinct stat fields" distinction within the single
 *       combat_gear bucket.
 *   D2: worst-case math — Math.max(...penalties). The editor surfaces a soft
 *       hint when >1 armour is worn (wording is concern #8 below).
 *   D2-FLOOR: floor at 0 lives ONLY at the helper composition site. STM overlay
 *       composes additively on top per ADR-004's no-bounds contract; the
 *       sheet renderer adds NO further clamp.
 *   D3: composition order — calcDefence(c) → subtract helper → floor → applyStMods.
 *   D4: STM overlay composes on top of c.derived.defence (the armour-adjusted
 *       base materialised by this module's materialiseDerivedDefence).
 *   D5: pure helper, symmetric with discAttrBonus.
 *
 * Concern #2 from ADR-006: the per-item armour annotation in editor/sheet.js:2240
 * must KEEP calling raw calcDefence(c). Its display intent is "if you wore only
 * this item, defence would be X" — a hypothetical pre-armour baseline, NOT the
 * live armour-adjusted value. Don't migrate that read site.
 *
 * Concern #9 from ADR-006: NO redundant floor clamps anywhere else (not in
 * applyStMods, not in the sheet renderer). The clamp lives in exactly one
 * place — the materialisation call below.
 */

import { calcDefence } from './accessors.js';
import { getCatalogueEntry } from './equipment-catalogue-cache.js';
// #896: meritEffectiveRating respects free dots / cp / xp / bonus channels.
// Used to detect Resources cap and Fixer presence without rewriting the
// accessor chain.
import { meritEffectiveRating } from '../editor/domain.js';

/**
 * EQC-1 review patch (issue #1152, Codex external review, 2026-08-13,
 * Pass 3b HIGH finding): the FIRST version of these predicates checked only
 * `armour_value != null` / `weapon_type != null`. That is too narrow - under
 * the OLD (pre-EQC-1) schema, bucket-specific fields were independently
 * nullable and never required as a set (ECM-1's own Non-Goal: "no per-bucket
 * schema validation"). A real legacy armour item could have `armour_value:
 * null` while still carrying a populated `defence_penalty`, or a legacy
 * weapon could have `weapon_type: null` while carrying `damage_mod`. A
 * single-field check silently drops such an item from armour/weapon
 * derivation the moment it is migrated to `combat_gear`, even though the
 * migration script reports success - the exact defect the review caught by
 * direct execution (`armour_value: null, defence_penalty: 2` -> penalty 0
 * instead of 2 after migration).
 *
 * These two predicates are the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for "is this
 * combat_gear entry armour-shaped / weapon-shaped" - every consumer
 * (armourDefencePenalty/wornArmourCount below, roll.js, roll-v2.js,
 * editor/sheet.js) imports and uses these rather than re-deriving its own
 * copy, so the discriminator can never drift out of sync between consumers
 * again the way it did in the first version of this story.
 */
export function isCombatGearArmourShaped(entry) {
  if (!entry) return false;
  return entry.armour_value != null || entry.defence_penalty != null;
}

export function isCombatGearWeaponShaped(entry) {
  if (!entry) return false;
  return entry.weapon_type != null || entry.damage_mod != null || entry.damage_type != null;
}

/**
 * EQC-2 (issue #1153, epic #1038) - "on me" (bonus applies in game) vs
 * "owned but elsewhere" (available in downtime only), per the epic's own
 * display distinction. Derived from the EXISTING `state` field, not a new
 * stored value - see the story's own Background for why a second
 * independent field was rejected (same "two things that can disagree" class
 * of bug the combat_gear shape check above needed fixing for).
 *
 * `carried`/`worn`/`active` = physically on the character = on me.
 * `stashed` = owned but elsewhere. `lost` = neither (the item is gone).
 *
 * NOTE: "on me" (possession) is BROADER than "bonus currently active" for
 * armour specifically, which additionally requires `state === 'worn'` (see
 * armourDefencePenalty above) - a carried-but-unworn breastplate is on you
 * but grants no AR. This predicate answers "is it near me right now", not
 * "is every possible bonus from it firing" - callers that need the latter
 * (armour) keep their own narrower check unchanged.
 *
 * Single source of truth for every consumer that previously re-derived this
 * exact three-state check inline (roll.js, roll-v2.js) - see EQC-1's own
 * isCombatGearArmourShaped/isCombatGearWeaponShaped for why duplicating this
 * kind of check per-consumer is the mistake to avoid.
 *
 * @param {object} item - a character's equipment[] entry (has `state`)
 * @returns {boolean}
 */
export function isEquipmentOnMe(item) {
  if (!item) return false;
  return item.state === 'carried' || item.state === 'worn' || item.state === 'active';
}

/**
 * Sum-by-worst-case of defence penalties from currently-worn armour.
 * Returns a non-negative integer (the magnitude — composition site subtracts).
 *
 * Per ADR-006 D2: worst-case stacking. Math.max of all qualifying penalties;
 * 0 when no qualifying armour is worn. Negative defence_penalty values are
 * non-sensical for armour and are filtered out before combination.
 *
 * Per ADR-006 D1: state === 'worn' is the only state that contributes. The
 * positive predicate is preferred over a not-stashed/not-lost shape because
 * a future state-enum addition would silently affect a negative predicate
 * (Concern #3).
 *
 * @param {object} c - character document
 * @param {function} [catalogueLookup] - (id) => catalogue entry | undefined.
 *   Default: the ECM-5 cache reader. Tests inject a synthetic map.
 * @returns {number} non-negative integer penalty magnitude
 */
export function armourDefencePenalty(c, catalogueLookup = getCatalogueEntry) {
  if (!c || !Array.isArray(c.equipment)) return 0;
  const penalties = [];
  for (const item of c.equipment) {
    if (!item || item.state !== 'worn') continue;
    const entry = catalogueLookup(item.catalogue_id);
    if (!entry || entry.bucket !== 'combat_gear' || !isCombatGearArmourShaped(entry)) continue;
    const p = Number.isInteger(entry.defence_penalty) ? entry.defence_penalty : 0;
    if (p > 0) penalties.push(p);
  }
  if (penalties.length === 0) return 0;
  return Math.max(...penalties);
}

/**
 * Count of armour items currently in state==='worn'. Drives the editor hint
 * surfaced when >1 armour is worn (ADR-006 D2 + Concern #8 — wording verbatim
 * in editor/sheet.js armour-section header).
 *
 * @param {object} c - character document
 * @param {function} [catalogueLookup]
 * @returns {number} count of worn armour items
 */
export function wornArmourCount(c, catalogueLookup = getCatalogueEntry) {
  if (!c || !Array.isArray(c.equipment)) return 0;
  let n = 0;
  for (const item of c.equipment) {
    if (!item || item.state !== 'worn') continue;
    const entry = catalogueLookup(item.catalogue_id);
    if (entry?.bucket === 'combat_gear' && isCombatGearArmourShaped(entry)) n++;
  }
  return n;
}

/**
 * Compute and materialise `c.derived.defence` per ADR-006 D3 + D4.
 *
 *   c.derived.defence = max(0, calcDefence(c) - armourDefencePenalty(c))
 *
 * This is the armour-adjusted base. applyStMods (called AFTER this, per the
 * render-path orchestrator) reads `c.derived.defence` as base, applies the
 * STM delta on top, and writes back — no longer the pre-ADR-006 bug where
 * applyStMods treated missing base as 0 (so STM mods on derived.defence
 * silently composed against 0 instead of the real mechanical base).
 *
 * Per ADR-006 D2-FLOOR + Concern #9: floor lives HERE, only HERE. No
 * defensive clamp in applyStMods or the sheet renderer.
 *
 * @param {object} c - character document (mutated)
 * @param {function} [catalogueLookup]
 * @returns {number} the materialised armour-adjusted defence (pre-overlay)
 */
export function materialiseDerivedDefence(c, catalogueLookup = getCatalogueEntry) {
  if (!c) return 0;
  const base = calcDefence(c);
  const penalty = armourDefencePenalty(c, catalogueLookup);
  const adjusted = Math.max(0, base - penalty);
  c.derived = c.derived || {};
  c.derived.defence = adjusted;
  return adjusted;
}

/**
 * Read-site helper: returns the modded c.derived.defence when it's been
 * materialised (the common case post-boot per the D8 cache-entry invariant);
 * falls back to a fresh armour-adjusted computation when not materialised
 * (edge cases — fresh chars, test contexts). The fallback is the same
 * computation materialiseDerivedDefence performs; the difference is whether
 * the result is cached on c.derived.defence or computed on the fly.
 *
 * Used by sheet.js, suite/sheet.js, roll calc, DT player pool, DT admin
 * resolution view — every consumer that previously called calcDefence(c)
 * directly migrates here.
 *
 * @param {object} c - character document
 * @param {function} [catalogueLookup]
 * @returns {number} displayed defence (overlay-modded if applicable)
 */
export function defenceForDisplay(c, catalogueLookup = getCatalogueEntry) {
  if (c && c.derived && typeof c.derived.defence === 'number') return c.derived.defence;
  if (!c) return 0;
  return Math.max(0, calcDefence(c) - armourDefencePenalty(c, catalogueLookup));
}

/**
 * Export-site helper: canonical mechanical defence (armour-adjusted, no
 * STM overlay). Always computes fresh — does NOT read c.derived.defence
 * which may carry an overlay-modded value at export time.
 *
 * Per ADR-004: STM overlays are scene-only adjustments and NOT canonical
 * character state. Character export (JSON / CSV / snapshot) captures the
 * mechanical baseline; overlays are a separate concern.
 *
 * @param {object} c - character document
 * @param {function} [catalogueLookup]
 * @returns {number} mechanical defence baseline (armour-adjusted)
 */
export function defenceMechanicalBase(c, catalogueLookup = getCatalogueEntry) {
  if (!c) return 0;
  return Math.max(0, calcDefence(c) - armourDefencePenalty(c, catalogueLookup));
}

// #896 — Equipment availability filter + Fixer errata (Peter 2026-06-18).
//
// Composition is simple subtraction with no overlay/scene-state interaction
// (per Khepri dispatch — no ADR needed). The helpers below are pure: take
// (item, c) → number / boolean. Read sites use them at render time; DT form
// uses them to gate dropdown affordability.
//
// Fixer errata: the 2-dot Social merit Fixer reduces the availability cost
// of all items by 1. Applies in all usage and displays — dropdown, sheet
// held-items, admin editor row labels (the admin editor BYPASSES the
// affordability gate but still SHOWS the reduced number for consistency).
//
// Out of scope (Peter / Khepri): admin catalogue page (ECM-6) shows raw
// catalogue availability; it is character-agnostic.
// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/**
 * Resources cap = effective rating of the character's Resources merit, or 0
 * if absent. Uses meritEffectiveRating so cp / xp / free / bonus channels
 * compose correctly without re-walking the merit array.
 *
 * @param {object} c - character document
 * @returns {number} resources rating (0-5)
 */
export function availabilityCap(c) {
  if (!c) return 0;
  const m = (c.merits || []).find(x => x?.name === 'Resources');
  return m ? meritEffectiveRating(c, m) : 0;
}

/**
 * Fixer reduction = 1 if the character has Fixer merit with effective rating
 * >= 1, else 0. The Fixer merit is a fixed 2-dot Social merit per the rules,
 * but we gate on the effective-rating check rather than mere presence so a
 * suppressed / zeroed Fixer entry (edge case during merit editing) doesn't
 * spuriously grant the reduction.
 *
 * @param {object} c - character document
 * @returns {0 | 1} reduction magnitude
 */
export function fixerReduction(c) {
  if (!c) return 0;
  const m = (c.merits || []).find(x => x?.name === 'Fixer');
  if (!m) return 0;
  return meritEffectiveRating(c, m) >= 1 ? 1 : 0;
}

/**
 * Effective availability of a catalogue item for a specific character:
 *
 *   effectiveAvailability(item, c) = max(0, item.availability - fixerReduction(c))
 *
 * Floored at 0 so a level-0 item with Fixer doesn't surface as -1; the
 * floor lives here, no clamp needed at consumer sites (same single-floor
 * discipline as ADR-006 Concern #9).
 *
 * `item` may be a catalogue entry (post-ECM-1 shape with `availability` int
 * field) OR a partial; null/undefined item or missing availability defaults
 * to 0.
 *
 * @param {object} item - catalogue entry
 * @param {object} c - character document
 * @returns {number} effective availability (0-5)
 */
export function effectiveAvailability(item, c) {
  const raw = Number.isInteger(item?.availability) ? item.availability : 0;
  return Math.max(0, raw - fixerReduction(c));
}

/**
 * Convenience wrapper: is the item within the character's affordability gate?
 *
 *   isAffordable(item, c) = effectiveAvailability(item, c) <= availabilityCap(c)
 *
 * Used by the DT form dropdown to disable unaffordable options. The admin
 * character editor explicitly BYPASSES this gate (ST override) but still
 * displays the effective availability per Peter's dispatch.
 *
 * @param {object} item - catalogue entry
 * @param {object} c - character document
 * @returns {boolean}
 */
export function isAffordable(item, c) {
  return effectiveAvailability(item, c) <= availabilityCap(c);
}

// ── Equipment renderer (EQ-2, issue #656) ────────────────────────────────────
// Renders catalogue-ref equipment[]. All buckets flow through the same array
// as of 2026-06-19 (character.assets[] retired).
// Edit mode shows the same view -- equipment is managed via the ST CRUD API (EQ-1).
//
// EQC-1 (issue #1152, epic #1038, 2026-08-13): re-partitioned from the old
// four buckets (weapon/armour/equipment/asset) to five (combat_gear/
// skill_gear/tool_utility/narrative/container). combat_gear merges the old
// weapon+armour buckets -- the Weapons/Armour section split below is now
// driven by which stat fields are POPULATED on the item (weapon_type/
// damage_mod = weapon-shaped; armour_value/defence_penalty = armour-shaped),
// not by a bucket comparison, since both shapes now share one bucket value.
// An item with neither shape populated (an ST entry with no stats filled in
// yet) falls to "Other Combat Gear" rather than being silently dropped.
export function shRenderEquipment(c, editMode) {
  const equip  = c.equipment || [];
  if (!editMode && !equip.length) return '';

  const STATE_LABELS = { carried: 'Carried', worn: 'Worn', stashed: 'Stashed', lost: 'Lost', active: 'Active' };
  const DMGTYPE      = { lethal: 'Lethal', bashing: 'Bashing', aggravated: 'Aggravated' };
  const WPNTYPE      = { melee: 'Melee', ranged: 'Ranged', thrown: 'Thrown' };
  const cycleLabel   = n  => n === 0 ? 'Pre-campaign' : `Cycle ${n}`;
  const stateChip    = st => `<span class="gen-granted-tag-view">${STATE_LABELS[st] || st}</span>`;
  // EQC-2 (issue #1153, epic #1038): "on me" (bonus applies in game) vs
  // "owned but elsewhere" (available in downtime only) — the epic's own
  // display distinction, computed from isEquipmentOnMe rather than a new
  // field. A `lost` item gets neither label (it's gone, not "elsewhere").
  // Rendered as a muted trait-qual fragment (this renderer's existing
  // convention for secondary info, e.g. item.notes) rather than a second
  // competing pill beside the state chip.
  const locationLabel = item => item.state === 'lost' ? null : (isEquipmentOnMe(item) ? 'On you' : 'Stored elsewhere');

  let h = '<div class="sh-sec"><div class="sh-sec-title">Equipment</div><div class="merit-list">';

  // Group equipment items by bucket, preserving flat-array index for remove buttons
  const byBucket = { combat_gear: [], skill_gear: [], tool_utility: [], narrative: [], container: [] };
  for (let i = 0; i < equip.length; i++) {
    const item   = equip[i];
    const entry  = getCatalogueEntry(item.catalogue_id) || {};
    const bucket = (entry.bucket && byBucket[entry.bucket]) ? entry.bucket : 'skill_gear';
    byBucket[bucket].push({ item, entry, idx: i });
  }

  // combat_gear sub-split by populated stat fields, not bucket (both shapes
  // now share the combat_gear bucket). An item matching neither shape (no
  // stats filled in) still renders, under "Other Combat Gear".
  // EQC-1 review patch (#1152): use the shared predicates from
  // equipment-derivation.js rather than a locally re-derived copy, so the
  // weapon/armour discriminator can never drift out of sync between this
  // renderer and armourDefencePenalty/the roll calculators again.
  const combatWeapons = byBucket.combat_gear.filter(x => isCombatGearWeaponShaped(x.entry));
  const combatArmour  = byBucket.combat_gear.filter(x => !isCombatGearWeaponShaped(x.entry) && isCombatGearArmourShaped(x.entry));
  const combatOther   = byBucket.combat_gear.filter(x => !isCombatGearWeaponShaped(x.entry) && !isCombatGearArmourShaped(x.entry));

  // ── Weapons ──
  if (combatWeapons.length) {
    h += '<div class="sh-sub-title">Weapons</div>';
    for (const { item, entry, idx } of combatWeapons) {
      const name  = entry.name || item.catalogue_id;
      // #896: per-character effective availability (raw - Fixer reduction).
      const eff = entry.availability != null ? effectiveAvailability(entry, c) : null;
      const parts = [
        entry.damage_mod != null ? `+${entry.damage_mod}` : null,
        DMGTYPE[entry.damage_type] || entry.damage_type || null,
        WPNTYPE[entry.weapon_type] || entry.weapon_type || null,
        eff != null ? `avail ${eff}` : null,
        locationLabel(item),
      ].filter(Boolean);
      const qual   = parts.join(' · ');
      const rmBtn  = editMode ? `<button class="sk-spec-rm" style="float:right;margin-top:2px" onclick="shRemoveEquip(${idx})" title="Remove">× Remove</button>` : '';
      h += `<div class="merit-plain"><div class="trait-row">` +
        `<div class="trait-main"><span class="trait-name">${esc(name)}</span><div class="trait-right">${stateChip(item.state)}${rmBtn}</div></div>` +
        `<div class="trait-sub">${qual ? `<span class="trait-qual">${esc(qual)}</span>` : ''}${item.notes ? `<span class="trait-qual dim">${esc(item.notes)}</span>` : ''}</div>` +
        `</div></div>`;
    }
  }

  // ── Armour ──
  if (combatArmour.length) {
    h += '<div class="sh-sub-title">Armour</div>';
    // Issue #879 (ADR-006 D2 + Concern #8): soft non-blocking hint when
    // multiple armour items are in state==='worn'. Stacking rule is
    // worst-case (Math.max of all defence_penalties); the hint exists so
    // an ST hitting a multi-worn debug case doesn't misinterpret the math.
    // Wording locked verbatim per Concern #8 — must not drift.
    if (wornArmourCount(c) > 1) {
      h += '<div class="sh-armour-hint" style="font-size:0.85em;opacity:0.75;margin-bottom:6px;">Only one armour applies; highest defence_penalty wins.</div>';
    }
    const baseDefence = calcDefence(c);
    for (const { item, entry, idx } of combatArmour) {
      const name  = entry.name || item.catalogue_id;
      // #896: per-character effective availability (raw - Fixer reduction).
      const eff = entry.availability != null ? effectiveAvailability(entry, c) : null;
      const parts = [
        entry.armour_value    != null ? `AR ${entry.armour_value}` : null,
        entry.defence_penalty != null ? `Defence ${baseDefence}(${baseDefence - entry.defence_penalty})` : null,
        eff != null ? `avail ${eff}` : null,
        locationLabel(item),
      ].filter(Boolean);
      const qual  = parts.join(' · ');
      const rmBtn = editMode ? `<button class="sk-spec-rm" style="float:right;margin-top:2px" onclick="shRemoveEquip(${idx})" title="Remove">× Remove</button>` : '';
      h += `<div class="merit-plain"><div class="trait-row">` +
        `<div class="trait-main"><span class="trait-name">${esc(name)}</span><div class="trait-right">${stateChip(item.state)}${rmBtn}</div></div>` +
        (qual || item.notes ? `<div class="trait-sub">${qual ? `<span class="trait-qual">${esc(qual)}</span>` : ''}${item.notes ? `<span class="trait-qual dim">${esc(item.notes)}</span>` : ''}</div>` : '') +
        `</div></div>`;
    }
  }

  // ── Other Combat Gear (combat_gear bucket, neither weapon- nor armour-shaped
  // — e.g. an ST entry with no stat fields filled in yet) ──
  if (combatOther.length) {
    h += '<div class="sh-sub-title">Other Combat Gear</div>';
    for (const { item, entry, idx } of combatOther) {
      const name  = entry.name || item.catalogue_id;
      const eff   = entry.availability != null ? effectiveAvailability(entry, c) : null;
      const qual  = [eff != null ? `avail ${eff}` : null, locationLabel(item)].filter(Boolean).join(' · ');
      const rmBtn = editMode ? `<button class="sk-spec-rm" style="float:right;margin-top:2px" onclick="shRemoveEquip(${idx})" title="Remove">× Remove</button>` : '';
      h += `<div class="merit-plain"><div class="trait-row">` +
        `<div class="trait-main"><span class="trait-name">${esc(name)}</span><div class="trait-right">${stateChip(item.state)}${rmBtn}</div></div>` +
        (qual || item.notes ? `<div class="trait-sub">${qual ? `<span class="trait-qual">${esc(qual)}</span>` : ''}${item.notes ? `<span class="trait-qual dim">${esc(item.notes)}</span>` : ''}</div>` : '') +
        `</div></div>`;
    }
  }

  // ── Skill Gear (old "Equipment" bucket, unchanged meaning) ──
  if (byBucket.skill_gear.length) {
    h += '<div class="sh-sub-title">Skill Gear</div>';
    for (const { item, entry, idx } of byBucket.skill_gear) {
      const name  = entry.name || item.catalogue_id;
      const pool  = (entry.skill_domain && entry.bonus_dice != null)
        ? `${entry.skill_domain} +${entry.bonus_dice} dice` : '';
      // #896: per-character effective availability (raw - Fixer reduction).
      const eff = entry.availability != null ? effectiveAvailability(entry, c) : null;
      const qualParts = [
        pool || null,
        eff != null ? `avail ${eff}` : null,
        locationLabel(item),
      ].filter(Boolean);
      const qual = qualParts.join(' · ');
      const rmBtn = editMode ? `<button class="sk-spec-rm" style="float:right;margin-top:2px" onclick="shRemoveEquip(${idx})" title="Remove">× Remove</button>` : '';
      h += `<div class="merit-plain"><div class="trait-row">` +
        `<div class="trait-main"><span class="trait-name">${esc(name)}</span><div class="trait-right">${stateChip(item.state)}${rmBtn}</div></div>` +

        `</div></div>`;
    }
  }

  // ── Tools / Utility (NEW bucket — "does a thing, no bonus") ──
  if (byBucket.tool_utility.length) {
    h += '<div class="sh-sub-title">Tools / Utility</div>';
    for (const { item, entry, idx } of byBucket.tool_utility) {
      const name  = entry.name || item.catalogue_id;
      const eff   = entry.availability != null ? effectiveAvailability(entry, c) : null;
      const parts = [entry.mechanical_effect || null, eff != null ? `avail ${eff}` : null, locationLabel(item)].filter(Boolean);

        `</div></div>`;
    }
  }

  // ── Narrative (NEW bucket — purely descriptive, no stat fields) ──
  if (byBucket.narrative.length) {
    h += '<div class="sh-sub-title">Narrative</div>';
    for (const { item, entry, idx } of byBucket.narrative) {
      const name  = entry.name || item.catalogue_id;
      const loc   = locationLabel(item);
      const rmBtn = editMode ? `<button class="sk-spec-rm" style="float:right;margin-top:2px" onclick="shRemoveEquip(${idx})" title="Remove">× Remove</button>` : '';

        `</div></div>`;
    }
  }

  // ── Containers (old "Assets" bucket — catalogue-backed since 2026-06-19) ──
  if (byBucket.container.length) {
    h += '<div class="sh-sub-title">Containers</div>';

        entry.mechanical_effect || null,
        eff != null ? `avail ${eff}` : null,
        cycleLabel(item.acquired_cycle),
      ].filter(Boolean);

      const rmBtn = editMode ? `<button class="sk-spec-rm" style="float:right;margin-top:2px" onclick="shRemoveEquip(${idx})" title="Remove">× Remove</button>` : '';

    }

    h += '<div class="sh-sub-title" style="margin-top:10px">Add Equipment Item</div>';

D:\Terra Mortis\TM Suite\archive\downtime_helper\README.md:114:This is the upsert key. When a CSV is uploaded, each row is looked up by `[active_cycle_id, character_name]`. If found and the hash matches, nothing is written. If found and changed, the record is updated and its child rows in `projects`, `sphere_actions`, and `contacts` are deleted and re-inserted wholesale. If not found, a new record is inserted. This means re-uploading a growing CSV is safe at any point before deadline.
D:\Terra Mortis\TM Suite\archive\downtime_helper\README.md:203:A **cycle** represents one downtime period (typically one month between games). Only one cycle is `active` at a time. The workflow is:
D:\Terra Mortis\TM Suite\archive\downtime_helper\README.md:205:1. The first CSV upload for a period auto-creates an active cycle named after the filename.
D:\Terra Mortis\TM Suite\archive\downtime_helper\README.md:206:2. Re-uploading the same or updated CSV upserts into the same active cycle.
D:\Terra Mortis\TM Suite\archive\downtime_helper\README.md:207:3. **New Cycle** closes the active cycle (status → `closed`) and creates a fresh one.

Roots grow towards what feeds them. Mia is behind the glass reading a paperback with no cover. She has torn it off, or it fell off, or she bought it that way, and you will never know which because you do not ask her questions.\nShe sells you the same seat she always sells you. She does not look up until she has finished her sentence, and when she does she nods once, the way a shopkeeper nods at someone who comes in at the same time every week and never needs to say what they want. You take the ticket. Your fingers do not touch.\nThe film is bad. You know it is bad because you have seen it before, twice, and it was bad both times, and you are here anyway because the alternative is not being here, and not being here means one fewer hour in a week where someone treats you as though you are simply a man who likes films. You watch the projector light catch the dust above the seats. You count the audience. There are eleven people, and none of them are watching each other, and the anonymity of a dark room full of strangers looking at the same bright rectangle is the closest thing you have to a congregation.\nMia is still reading when you leave. She does not say goodnight and you do not say thank you, and this small mutual silence is the most honest transaction you will have this month.\n\n## The Academy\n\nThe Academy is yours and this month it rewards attention. The pubs through Camperdown and Newtown are keeping their doors open later, the laneways around Victoria Park stay busy past midnight, and the blood you take from stragglers on quiet backstreets off Abercrombie comes up full-bodied and reliable. Four others work this territory alongside you. Doc twice, Keeper twice, Cyrus and Mac once each. You cross none of them in the act, which is as it should be. What threads through the territory is harder to place. On Carillon Avenue a pedestrian you pass agrees readily with a remark you did not make, and further down toward Missenden Road a couple in a parked car forget, between one sentence and the next, what they were arguing about.\n\n## We Own the Night\n\nYour role in the ritual is the seed-bearing. Across the evening, you move among the attendees who have been chosen in advance and you plant what the ritual will bloom into. A Seed of Her Divinity in each of them, dropped through touch or gaze, specific to the night they are having, specific to the Her they are being offered to. Your Fires of Inspiration burns at nine-again across the work. By the end of the ceremony, the seeded attendees are carrying a piece of the evening in them, the kind that will flower later, the kind that will remember itself at odd hours of the weeks to come. They will evangelise without realising that is what they are doing. The Crone's reach expands by every one of them.\n\n## Keeping it Tight!\n\nYou work the Academy across four weekends and two weeknights and by the end of the month you have the map you wanted. Keeper walks the King Street stretches and leaves no attempt at concealment; the two of you cross six times and neither of you ever slows. Mac covers the abattoir-approach lanes the way a man walks home from work. Cyrus runs the evenings through the bar staff and door crews, which you register first as a rumour moving the wrong direction through a venue and then as the texture of who was at which booth. Doc is on the clinic side of the territory and her circuit overlaps the hospital approaches. Five feeders walked your ground this month. Keeper and Doc twice each, Cyrus once, Mac once. The visible ones. Two others used concealment well enough that what you have is negative space rather than a face, a stretch of Wilson Street that is quieter than it should be and a table at a bar on King Street that was cleared without anyone remembering who cleared it. The territory itself is on the move. Someone has been running a glossy rumour campaign through the inner-west weeklies and the sort of Reddit threads that shape how a neighbourhood talks about itself, the push big enough that you can put a name to the hand. Brandy LaRoux. The other pushes are smaller and the attribution is looser; somebody has been seeding occult flavour, someone else is leaning gently on the academic rooms, and somebody further out is pulling in the opposite direction, a quiet subtraction that shows up as one fewer venue filing a late-trading application than you would expect. You file it and walk home.\n\n## An Eye for\n\nThe ritual is the one your sire taught you by example and the example was not gentle. You cut out your own eye in a clean room under good lighting and the pain is a different class of pain than you remember. You bind the eye to the lens of a Panasonic AG-UX180 with vitae and the kind of whispered words that Moulding Room uses instead of a rulebook. When the feeds come up on the monitors afterwards, you do not see through the camera. You are the camera. It is different to seeing. It is dirtier than seeing. You find you like it.\n\n## The Panopticon\n\nThe Hub Theatre locks in the morning you make the call. The venue looks the way you wanted it to look, and better. What you are likely to capture of Court on the night itself may be far less than you had hoped for, as your Kindred read the space better than any Kine. You do not tell him what you think because what you think would require you to explain more of what you are than he can safely know, and besides, he is not asking for your opinion, he is asking to be heard.\nHe finishes the schnitzel. He closes the notebook. He laughs, briefly, the laugh of a man who knows that is not true but appreciates the sentiment, and you sit with him in the booth until the bar lights start their slow decline towards closing.\n\n## The Second City\n\nThe tags are landing. You walk the Second City most nights, tracing the routes you pick for the graffiti teams, and by the third week the message is settling into the street's own grammar: a glyph near the Parramatta Square overpass, a phrase painted high on a fire exit off Church Street, a small white paste-up tucked into the corner of a bookshop window near Westfield Parramatta. The mortals are reading them without knowing they are reading them. The territory hums. Feeding has gone well enough that you have had to space your cycles more carefully than before; there is abundance, and abundance brings its own discipline problem. You note where the glyphs are landing and where they are being painted over, and you note who does the painting over, and you file it.\n\n## Night of the Long Spoons\n\nThe invitation to Keeper is a small test and he accepts it, which is a good sign. You walk him through your territory across the evening the way you walk somebody through your own rooms, showing him the Carthian way of doing this. Feeding for you is slow, relational, it requires the acquaintance before it requires the throat. You take what you need from three people across three venues and none of them think the evening has been anything other than pleasant. Keeper watches and does not comment. Then it is his turn and you watch. He takes you to nursing homes, getting in with Dominate and Obfuscate. There he seeks out the loneliest people, rouse them from slumber and hear their stories. He takes only a single Vitae per kine, commenting on their frailty, they are old after all, then he uses Dominate to wipe your visit from their minds, leave them with wonderful memories of being visited by a long-lost lover or friend with an understanding that it was likely the last time they can visit. These people will die in time, but their lives shall live on in him; it is a gift, at least to his thinking. But you start to realised why he seems so unstable, fuck knows how many lives he remembers. He has lived around 300 years, but he probably has memories of millions of years, thousands and thousands of lives. You wonder if that insanity is something that can be weaponised for your benefit. Afterwards, you go to Riverside Theaters, and watch a local indigenous circus performance. Perhaps an indulgence, but he waxes on about the wonders of the culture that is the memory of this land and his admiration of The Dreaming. You are not sure you understand this threat any more than you did before, but you certainly know more.\n\n## Tuning in to Cityscapes\n\nYou roam Sydney at the pace of somebody listening. Tegan Groves. Resident of nowhere around here, which makes her a poacher, which makes her interesting. You note the pattern of her circuit. Conrad crosses your cordon twice and does not register you, which means either he is not looking or his method is not pitched at what you are. Sister Hazel's attempt at domination on a man you had already pinned as a poacher gets her in the middle of the only fight you have to break up this month, and it is a clean fight because she wins it. The territory's larger shape resolves into a tug-of-war. Somebody is building quietly, moving money into buildings and contracts; somebody else is pulling just as hard the other way, draining investment, withdrawing backers, creating the soft vacuum that makes a neighbourhood feel abandoned. The territory is sliding despite both hands, and you suspect the overfeeding pressure is doing the work neither of them can undo. St Dom's own hand is visible here and there, a steadying touch on the social rooms that keeps the month from being worse.\n\n## It Sure Is Dockyards Around Here\n\nThe tracksuit goes on after dusk and the bop comes down late. You work the container approaches around Botany Road and the laneways off Bourke Road, and by the second week you are picking the nights by the shape of the trouble. A man with a knife going into a corner shop will be on the ground with the knife in a storm drain before he has finished forming the sentence he rehearsed. The costume, such as it is, never shows a face. Familiar Stranger carries the mask when Familiar Stranger needs to. A phone-camera still has been passed around a local Facebook group: a silhouette against a warehouse wall, the caption calling you the Tracksuit Terror. René St. Dominique sends word through an intermediary, the kind of message that says nothing and acknowledges everything. What you feel on the streets you patrol is not the territory rising. It is the territory holding its ground against a current that is pulling it under, and the ground you hold is yours.\n\n## Continue! The work carries you a half-step further than the material wants to be pushed, and after that the hours of effort give you diminishing return. By month's end you have an upgrade to show for the work and a problem to solve if you want to go any further. A Seed of Her Divinity in each of them, dropped through touch or gaze, specific to the night they are having, specific to the Her they are being offered to. Your Fires of Inspiration burns at nine-again across the work. By the end of the ceremony, the seeded attendees are carrying a piece of the evening in them, the kind that will flower later, the kind that will remember itself at odd hours of the weeks to come. They will evangelise without realising that is what they are doing. The Crone's reach expands by every one of them.\n\n## Keeping it Tight!\n\nYou work the Academy across four weekends and two weeknights and by the end of the month you have the map you wanted. Keeper walks the King Street stretches and leaves no attempt at concealment; the two of you cross six times and neither of you ever slows. Doc is on the clinic side of the territory and her circuit overlaps the hospital approaches. Five feeders walked your ground this month. Keeper and Doc twice each, Cyrus once, Mac once. The visible ones. Two others used concealment well enough that what you have is negative space rather than a face, a stretch of Wilson Street that is quieter than it should be and a table at a bar on King Street that was cleared without anyone remembering who cleared it. The territory itself is on the move. You file it and walk home.\n\n## An Eye for\n\nThe ritual is the one your sire taught you by example and the example was not gentle. You cut out your own eye in a clean room under good lighting and the pain is a different class of pain than you remember. You find you like it.\n\n## The Panopticon\n\nThe Hub Theatre locks in the morning you make the call. The stretch between Green Square and Mascot has gone quieter after ten in a way that unsettles the palate as much as the blood does. Whole blocks along Botany Road lie empty at hours that used to be busy. You cross the same stretch of footpath twice and cannot remember, either time, which direction you were walking. Mortals in the pubs go silent about certain streets without knowing why.\n\n## The Barrens\n\nThe Barrens do not belong to anyone and the silence is the sound of that. You take the train north as far as the line runs and then a hire car past where the streetlights thin, out to the retreat centres and the unaccredited missions that sit at the edge of the maps the diocese will publicise. The blood you take is the blood of a man who had been running a retreat programme for a decade and the confessions he took from it, and the palate of it is clean in a way the Dockyards have not been for weeks. There is nobody else out here. No acknowledgement to offer, no trade of nods, no ledger. On the drive back the suburbs thicken around you and the city you serve begins to press against the windscreen again.\n\n## Arms of the Abyss\n\nYou spend the month deep in your own shadow. The discipline does not come by study alone; it comes by a kind of obedience to the dark in you, a willingness to let it move as an extension of your own reach. You sit with it. You practise the first reaches in the basement of the cathedral storehouse, the dark thickening around your hands the way wet cloth thickens, then finally taking the shape you have been asking it to take. By month's end the shadows answer. Not fluently. But they answer.\n\n## Loafs\n\nYou know which men at which parishes are the ones to watch before the month begins, and across four weekends you confirm what your instinct already told you. The boy who runs the youth outreach at St Bede's and has been asked to stop meeting one of the altar-servers alone. A deacon in Alexandria who has a tone with the women of the congregation that the women would not use themselves. You take one each, across the month, in circumstances they will not be able to reconstruct. What the work confirms for you is uglier than what you hoped for. There is too much of it. Sydney without the Lance has let this kind of thing bloom across the parishes in a way that turns your stomach. The feeding is easy and the reason it is easy is a grievance.\n\n## Fishes\n\nThe second set of nights extends the first. The same work, the same calculus, the same stomach-turn at how easy the pickings are. A Presbyterian elder whose authority over his women's group has slipped past pastoral into something else. A seminary-trained self-styled spiritual counsellor in Macdonaldtown who has built a private congregation of vulnerable adults. By month's end you have fed more often than you planned and you have fed on a class of people you did not expect to have this much of in any single district. The grievance you began with has not diminished. It has been catalogued.\n\n## In our Father's House\n\nThe old Lance records give up what they can and you work through them across the month, the books you already own and the contacts in the covenant who have kept their own. The pattern that emerges points to one place more than any other. St Mary's Cathedral near Hyde Park sits at the centre of everything the Lance once held in this city. You mark it and pause there. It is a large place, active, still a working cathedral, and the work of walking in to see what remains is not the same as the work of reading about it. With the work Nicolle helped collate things suggest that there is more to the area, something substantial, something subterranean.\n\n## Retainer\n\nNicole handles the overflow. The correspondence that accumulates across a month of active research, the archive requests, the scheduling with two retired Jesuits who will only meet on Tuesdays, the quiet follow-ups with diocesan record-keepers who have misfiled what they promised to pull. She manages all of it without consulting you. While Mentors can be highly competent, they almost always want something in return for their services. The dot rating determines the Mentor's capabilities, and to what extent he'll aid your character. When establishing a Mentor, determine what the Mentor wants from your character. This should be personally important to him, and it should reflect on the dot rating chosen. A one-dot Mentor might be incapable of dealing with modern society, and want to live vicariously through your character. This might mean coming to him and telling stories of her exploits. A five-dot Mentor would want something astronomical, such as an oath to procure an ancient, cursed artifact that may or may not exist, in order to prevent a prophesized death. Choose three Skills the Mentor possesses. You can substitute Resources for one of these Skills. Once per session, the character may ask her Mentor for a favour. The favour must involve one of those Skills, or be within the scope of his Resources. The Mentor commits to the favour (often asking for a commensurate favour in return), and if a roll is required, the Mentor is automatically considered to have successes equal to his dot rating. Alternately, you may ask the Storyteller to have the Mentor act on your character's behalf, without her character knowing or initiating the request. Mystery Cult Initiation (● to ●●●●●) Cults are far more common than people would like to admit. "Mystery cult" is the catch-all term for a phenomenon ranging from secret societies couched in fraternity houses, to scholarly cabals studying the magic of classical symbolism, to mystical suicide cults to the God-Machine. Mystery Cult Initiation reflects membership in one of these esoteric groups. The dot rating dictates standing. One dot is an initiate, two a respected member, three a priest or organizer, four a decision-making leader, and five is a high priest or founder. If you wish your character to begin play in a cult, work with your Storyteller to develop the details. Designing a Mystery Cult requires three things, at bare minimum. First is a Purpose. This is the defining reason 52 the face in the mirror-Characters Sample Cults Sample Cult: The Chosen of Mammon Mammon believes in the almighty dollar, and its inherent power. Followers of Mammon are expected to obtain material wealth and power at any cost. Fortunately, their networks help initiates quickly claim promotions and transfers into more prominent areas of influence. Cultists: Hedge fund manager, mailboy on a mission, outsourcer, personal assistant to the stars, talent scout, third generation CEO Initiation Benefits ● All initiates learn to cut through red tape to fulfil their later duties. They gain a Politics Speciality in Bureaucracy. ●● Full members must learn to speak, read, and write in Aramaic. They gain the Language Merit (Aramaic) free of charge. ●●● As a cultist delves into the mysteries of Mammon, she gains access to greater cult resources. Spend two dots between Contacts, Allies, Resources, or Retainers reflecting this relationship. ●●●● The self-centred and power-obsessed priests of Mammon gain the Thief of Fate (●●●) Merit. For this reason, priests are prohibited from touching other cultists. ●●●●● The high priestess of Mammon benefits from the tithes of her already wealthy followers. She gains three dots of Resources. Additionally, she may make a Resources ●●●●● purchase once per month without limitation, by drawing from the cult's coffers. Sample Cult: Sisters of the Machine Gun, Brothers of the Bomb The Brothers and Sisters band together with their rudimentary understanding of something they call "the God-Machine" in order to prevent its ascendancy to whatever mysterious power it strives for. They've repurposed artifacts and reverse-engineered their power into more technological weapons to fight back the darkness. The Brothers and Sisters tend toward universities and other places of learning, where a bit of esoteric knowledge can bleed through the mundane and open eyes to the truths of the universe. Cultists: God-Machine survivor, librarian-turned-networker, militant defender (Sister Machine Gun), second-generation mentor, tech expert (Brother Bomb) Initiation Benefits ● New recruits, while not yet trusted, receive training to better spot the influence of the God-Machine. They gain an Occult Speciality in The God-Machine. ●● Small cells of the Brothers and Sisters network through a handful of active initiates. For this reason, all initiates gain Contacts ● (Brothers and Sisters) free of charge. ●●● Respected initiates that have proven they're likely to survive more than a few years are taught the secrets of repurposing holy artifacts into weapons. By destroying such an artifact, they can give one weapon the ability to hurt spirits and ghosts. ●●●● At higher ranks within the organization, members are assigned wards and students. Take three dots in Retainers, allocated as the player sees fit (that is, one three-dot Retainer, three one-dot Retainers, etc.). ●●●●● The highest-ranking Brothers and Sisters were mostly first contact survivors. They've seen more of the God-Machine's influence than most anyone still standing. They gain a modified version of the Encyclopaedic Knowledge Merit relating directly to the God-Machine. the cult exists. Usually it's tied in with the cult's history and recent background. Invictus Oaths Invictus Oaths are the First Estate's ace in the hole, its way of establishing and maintaining a rigid and effective hierarchy. An Invictus Notary officiates Oaths; a character with the Notary Merit can preside over any Oath, so long as the participants meet the prerequisites for the Merit. Recognized and manumitted Invictus must have at least one active Oath. This is to say Invictus require the presence of a Notary for their induction. Each Oath is a two-way street, with two active participants: the liege and vassal. The vassal must purchase the Oath Merit to gain its advantages; the liege does not. When swearing an Oath, the participants must define terms in addition to the Oath's effects. Usually, they swear for a finite time, often a year and a day. Terms include conditions for violation, which end the contract (and the Oath's effects) immediately. Unless otherwise noted, the vassal does not have to be Invictus; in fact, most are not. In rare cases, ghouls or other mortals enter Oaths. Most Notaries refuse to preside over such agreements. Typically, Oaths are temporary. Merit dots revert when the Oath ends; see The Sanctity of Merits on p. 109.

One day you will lead with the important thing, and I will need to sit down from the shock of it.\nSo you have a position at your club. People are apparently looking to you for something, and you are handling this by being nervous about it in writing to your family instead of telling anyone there that you are nervous about it. I recognise this because I have watched you do it your entire adult life. You collect responsibilities the way other people collect receipts, quietly and without telling anyone, and then you are surprised when the pile gets heavy.\nThe other thing you mentioned, about the people talking about bringing back the old ways, the old guard: I know what that sounds like to you. I know what it does to your shoulders and your jaw. You get that from Dad, who once argued with a man at a petrol station for twenty minutes about something that turned out to be a misunderstanding, and did not apologise afterwards because he said the principle still stood.\nBut you are there now, Alice. You chose to be there. If something needs saying, say it to the people in the room, not to me in an email at two in the morning.\nDad asks if you are eating. I am not going to pass on his exact words because they were mostly about soup.\n\n## Touchstone\n\nYour sister's phone buzzes three times during the walk from the car to the restaurant, and she answers none of them. This is how you know she has been looking forward to seeing you: she has decided, for the duration of the evening, that nobody else exists. She does this rarely and only for people she considers worth the silence, and you have never once taken it for granted.\nShe picks the place, because she always picks the place, and it is a small Vietnamese restaurant on a side street in Marrickville where the menus are laminated and the woman behind the counter remembers her order from last time. Your sister finds this deeply satisfying. She tells you about it twice: once when you sit down and once when the food arrives, as though the continuity of being remembered by a stranger is proof that the world is functioning correctly.\nYou order something you will not eat and move it around the plate with enough conviction that she does not notice. She is telling you about a colleague who has been promoted above his competence, and her analysis of his failings is thorough, specific, and delivered with the calm precision of someone who has been composing this speech in her head for weeks. You ask one question and she talks for another ten minutes, and the relief of being in the presence of someone who requires nothing from you except an audience is so uncomplicated that you almost forget the small rituals: the sip of water, the nod, the laugh at the right moment.\nShe steals a prawn off your plate without asking, which she has done since you were fourteen, and you let her, which you have done for exactly as long.\n\n## The North Shore\n\nThe Shore is at the top of its game and you feel it every way a resident can. Military Road carries confident crowds past eleven. The restaurants in Kirribilli and the bars behind Crows Nest are running late, and foot traffic along the harbour stretches is the healthy kind. Blood comes up clean but the palate catches the faint trace of other feeders having been through ahead of you, nothing wrong with it yet, only a ledger opening. Five of your own are drawing from the territory this month, and three others are feeding here without your grant. Cyrus has been at it without asking. Ivana has been through twice. Wan Yelong is working the lecture crowd with the quiet confidence of somebody who does not think permission applies to him. Past the Oaks on a Tuesday a stranger in the queue behind you is paying closer attention than strangers usually do, and on Willoughby Road you pass through a stretch of pavement that feels listened to.\n\n## Keeping it Tight! (Alice version, credit to Jack)\n\nYou walk the North Shore across four nights, varying your route each time. Brandy takes the harbourside paths with the slow deliberate stride of someone who wants to be noticed, and you cross her circuit twice without needing to coordinate it. Charlie is impossible to track, but notifies you that it is covering the commercial stretches around Military Road with workmanlike efficiency, and you catch the edges of Ivana's movement twice near Cremorne Point.\nThe territory is busy. You count at least six other Kindred feeding here over the course of the month, which is a lot of mouths for one stretch of shoreline. Wan Yelong feeds amongst the harbourside lecture crowd with the quiet confidence of someone who has been doing this for a very long time. Yusuf works the late-night bars with an intensity that leaves a mark on the atmosphere even after he has moved on. One feeder you cannot place at all; you sense the traces of their passage but never see them directly, which tells you something about their methods.\nCyrus you spot twice, feeding in the North Shore without having sought your permission. He is not hiding it.\n\n## Happy Cult\n\nYou spend the month tending the people you have collected. A luncheon at the Mosman house on the second Sunday. A private reading group midweek. Two one-on-one conversations with members who have been anxious about the way the last few weeks have felt, and whose anxiety is useful to register rather than to dismiss. The paranoia is higher this cycle than you remember it being, and the paranoia is the bond. The cult closes around itself. Your base and your people are yours.\n\n## We Own the Night\n\nYour contribution is the oldest trick any of you know. Mantle of Amorous Fire layered into the ritual circle so that everyone who takes up the Cruac's invitation wears the Blush of Life for the night. You lead the portion of the chant that unlocks it. When it takes, a room full of Kindred suddenly breathes, flushes, warms at the skin, is confusable with the mortals on the dance floor below. The dancers who are paying attention take this as a miracle. The ones who are not paying attention take it as the DJ getting the drop right. She learned from your notes rather than from mine, which I know because she makes the same mistake with the third invocation that you used to make, and I have chosen not to correct her because watching you both get it wrong in exactly the same way has become one of the small pleasures of my evenings.\nThe coven stands. The roof still leaks in the same corner. I mention this because you asked if they were well, and the answer is that they are exactly as they were when you left, which is the most honest measure of wellness I can offer.\nYour garden will take time. The soil in that country does not know our blood yet, and it will refuse you before it accepts you, and then it will refuse you again because it has forgotten that it already accepted you. This is not a failing on your part. It is how soil works when it has not been spoken to in eighty years. Cut your hands on it as many times as necessary. The plants do not care about your comfort; they care about your persistence.\nYou write about the angry lady in the ocean and the old temple and the borders in the same paragraph, as though they are all one problem. They are not. You know this, because you separated them in your next sentence, but I want to be clear: walk the borders first, tend the garden second, and leave the dreaming until your feet are planted somewhere solid. The old temple has waited this long and it will wait for you.\nYour Maiden Alice sounds young and recently burdened. Do not let her carry weight she has not been taught to hold. Teach her the practical things before you teach her the sacred ones, because the practical things are what will keep her standing when the sacred ones become heavy.\nI am where I have always been. The roof leaks. The coven persists. Write when you can, and write longer when you do.\n\n## Touchstone\n\nKateryna cannot sleep and has come to find you about it, carrying the blanket from her bed in a bundle against her chest as though it were something she had rescued. She stands in the doorway and announces this fact with the grave authority of a child who considers sleeplessness a serious injustice that someone ought to address.\nYou are sitting on the floor with a half-finished piece of embroidery across your knee, and you move it aside without comment to make room for her. She settles next to you, arranges the blanket into a nest around her legs, and watches your hands work the needle for a while with the particular intensity of a child who is pretending not to be tired.\nShe asks what you are making. You tell her it is a ribbon for a friend. She asks if the friend is nice, and you say yes, and she asks if the friend is here in Sydney, and you say yes, and she asks if Sydney is going to be home now, and you do not answer that one immediately because the question is larger than she knows.\nYou thread a new colour instead, a red that catches the lamplight, and she leans against your arm with the full unthinking weight of a child who has decided you are furniture. Her breathing slows. The embroidery takes shape under your hands: a pattern your grandmother taught you, carried across borders and decades and one particular kind of death, and now stitched into a ribbon in a rented house in a country where the soil does not yet know your name.\nKateryna is asleep before you finish the first repeat of the pattern. You do not move your arm.\n\n## The Barrens\n\nThe land around Ku-ring-gai does not belong to you and it does not pretend to. You have lived here for two months now and the bush has accepted your presence the way it accepts anything that does not try to change it: with indifference and the constant quiet reminder that you are a guest in something older than your kind.\nThe garden is taking root slowly, and the soil resists you exactly the way your sire said it would. You have cut your hands on the local plants often enough that you have stopped noticing the sting, and the first shoots of what you planted last month have survived, which is not the same as thriving but is enough to keep going.\nThe strange figures you glimpsed last month on the paths toward Pittwater are still there, or others like them. You catch the edges of their movement on two occasions this month: once at dusk near the fire trail above McCarrs Creek, once on the road down to Church Point. They move through the bush with a sureness that is not human and not Kindred and not animal, and they are very good at not being where you are looking by the time you look. You have decided not to follow them yet, because the land they are moving towards does not feel like it wants you to.\nThe blood this month came from the rave in the Academy rather than from the bush, which was a relief your body registered even if you did not intend to acknowledge it. Animal blood sustains, but it does not satisfy, and the difference between the two is something you are learning to carry without complaint.\n\n## Patrolling the Academy\n\nYou walk the Academy across four nights and what you come back with is the feeling more than the detail. Jack is out on the territory and you know this because the territory carries the quality of being attended to. One other patroller crosses your path near Victoria Park, a brief mutual acknowledgement and nothing more. The Beast's Hackles prickle twice on King Street where the occult shops have been busier than they should be, and once near a laneway behind Enmore Theatre where somebody has been standing for a long time without moving. You file the impressions and leave the analysis to those who patrol with more than instinct.\n\n## Patrolling the Shore\n\nThe North Shore is less familiar ground and your patrol reads it that way, in fragments rather than in the full picture. Alice is on the territory and you feel her the way you feel any Regent walking her own ground, a settled presence that tells you the territory is already watched. Brandy you catch once on Military Road, striding with the confidence of somebody who wants to be seen. The foot traffic is healthy and late and the blood would come up clean if you were feeding here. Two faces you do not place pass you near Cremorne Point, moving with the disinterest of people who are very interested in not being interesting.\n\n## Party Party Party\n\nYour part of the ritual is the oldest part and the quietest. While Cyrus holds the beat and Jack seeds the crowd and Keeper works the gantry above, you move through the room at floor level with your hands open and your Cruac running low and steady. What you are doing is not visible. It sits underneath everything else. You are weaving predatory confidence into the feeding, stitching a safety net under the bacchanal so that every Crone who reaches for blood tonight reaches with certainty. The Divination in you reads the room as it tips, each feeder's moment arriving a half-beat before they know it will, and you hold the pattern until the last of them has taken what they need. Four successes. The net holds cleanly. Nobody frenzies who should not frenzy. Nobody feeds who should not feed. Your contribution is invisible and that is exactly how you prefer it.\n\n## For the Others\n\nYou gather the honey yourself from a native bee colony in a park near the Academy, which takes the better part of a night and most of your patience. The shawl is one of your second-tier pieces, still good, still carrying the work of your hands. The pearls you add because the gesture needs weight. The kangaroo vine with fruit still on it you cut from a fence-line in Stanmore, the leaves glossy and dark. You place the offering near where you saw them last, arranged on a flat stone with the deliberateness of somebody who knows how to make an offering and who is choosing, very carefully, not to presume she knows who she is offering to. You come back twice a week across the month. The first visit, nothing has changed. The second, the honey is gone. The shawl has been moved. The pearls remain. On the third visit the vine has been replaced with a different cutting, one you did not plant, its leaves darker than any kangaroo vine you have seen in this city. Somebody has accepted the opening. Somebody has replied.\n\n## Retainer\n\nYour people do as they are told. A very nice shovel arrives by the end of the week, the handle wrapped in soft leather, the blade practical and sturdy. She does not look up until she has finished her sentence, and when she does she nods once, the way a shopkeeper nods at someone who comes in at the same time every week and never needs to say what they want. You take the ticket. Your fingers do not touch.\nThe film is bad. You know it is bad because you have seen it before, twice, and it was bad both times, and you are here anyway because the alternative is not being here, and not being here means one fewer hour in a week where someone treats you as though you are simply a man who likes films. You watch the projector light catch the dust above the seats. You count the audience. There are eleven people, and none of them are watching each other, and the anonymity of a dark room full of strangers looking at the same bright rectangle is the closest thing you have to a congregation.\nMia is still reading when you leave. She does not say goodnight and you do not say thank you, and this small mutual silence is the most honest transaction you will have this month.\n\n## The Academy\n\nThe Academy is yours and this month it rewards attention. The pubs through Camperdown and Newtown are keeping their doors open later, the laneways around Victoria Park stay busy past midnight, and the blood you take from stragglers on quiet backstreets off Abercrombie comes up full-bodied and reliable. Four others work this territory alongside you. Doc twice, Keeper twice, Cyrus and Mac once each. You cross none of them in the act, which is as it should be. What threads through the territory is harder to place. On Carillon Avenue a pedestrian you pass agrees readily with a remark you did not make, and further down toward Missenden Road a couple in a parked car forget, between one sentence and the next, what they were arguing about.\n\n## We Own the Night\n\nYour role in the ritual is the seed-bearing. Across the evening, you move among the attendees who have been chosen in advance and you plant what the ritual will bloom into. A Seed of Her Divinity in each of them, dropped through touch or gaze, specific to the night they are having, specific to the Her they are being offered to. Your Fires of Inspiration burns at nine-again across the work. By the end of the ceremony, the seeded attendees are carrying a piece of the evening in them, the kind that will flower later, the kind that will remember itself at odd hours of the weeks to come. They will evangelise without realising that is what they are doing. The Crone's reach expands by every one of them.\n\n## Keeping it Tight!\n\nYou work the Academy across four weekends and two weeknights and by the end of the month you have the map you wanted. Keeper walks the King Street stretches and leaves no attempt at concealment; the two of you cross six times and neither of you ever slows. Mac covers the abattoir-approach lanes the way a man walks home from work. Cyrus runs the evenings through the bar staff and door crews, which you register first as a rumour moving the wrong direction through a venue and then as the texture of who was at which booth. Doc is on the clinic side of the territory and her circuit overlaps the hospital approaches. Five feeders walked your ground this month. Keeper and Doc twice each, Cyrus once, Mac once. The visible ones. Two others used concealment well enough that what you have is negative space rather than a face, a stretch of Wilson Street that is quieter than it should be and a table at a bar on King Street that was cleared without anyone remembering who cleared it. The territory itself is on the move. Someone has been running a glossy rumour campaign through the inner-west weeklies and the sort of Reddit threads that shape how a neighbourhood talks about itself, the push big enough that you can put a name to the hand. Brandy LaRoux. The other pushes are smaller and the attribution is looser; somebody has been seeding occult flavour, someone else is leaning gently on the academic rooms, and somebody further out is pulling in the opposite direction, a quiet subtraction that shows up as one fewer venue filing a late-trading application than you would expect. You file it and walk home.\n\n## An Eye for\n\nThe ritual is the one your sire taught you by example and the example was not gentle. You cut out your own eye in a clean room under good lighting and the pain is a different class of pain than you remember. You bind the eye to the lens of a Panasonic AG-UX180 with vitae and the kind of whispered words that Moulding Room uses instead of a rulebook. When the feeds come up on the monitors afterwards, you do not see through the camera. You are the camera. It is different to seeing. It is dirtier than seeing. You find you like it.\n\n## The Panopticon\n\nThe Hub Theatre locks in the morning you make the call. The owner takes the lease terms without haggling, and by the end of the first week the cameras and microphones are running through a rig you have built yourself, feeds routed through two layers of encryption into a room only you hold the key to. The venue looks the way you wanted it to look, and better. What you are likely to capture of Court on the night itself may be far less than you had hoped for, as your Kindred read the space better than any Kine. But the bones of a surveillance practice are now yours, and the Hub Theatre is yours to set the lighting on.\n\n## Allies (Police) ***\n\nYour police allies are permanent feelers across the Academy's night-shift roster. Across the month they feed you the short list of incidents that deserve a second look from the angle you are looking from. Two stand out. A woman walked into a St Peters ED with puncture wounds consistent with animal attack she could not describe; her statement was logged and shelved. A man on Wilson Street was assaulted by somebody who left no trace on the CCTV coverage of the block. Neither case is being actively pursued. You file both and put them on the watch-list for next cycle.\n\n## Allies (High Society) ***\n\nYour high-society people handle the owner the way high-society people handle owners of closed theatres, which is with deference and money. The Hub Theatre in Newtown is yours for the night of Court. By week four the phrase \"the shadows are watching\" has shown up on a Reddit thread that was not yours to begin with. The seed has taken.\n\n## Allies (Occult) ***\n\nYour occult people feed the other side of the wheel. Tarot shops along King Street have queues on Wednesday nights. Two bars off Wilson Street have put spooky-named cocktails on the menu. A card-reader you have met twice sends you a thank-you note on thick paper, the handwriting deliberate, saying only that the air has opened up around her table. You file it.\n\n## Cacophony Savvy 1\n\nA phone-camera still has been doing the rounds on a Mascot community Facebook group. A silhouette against a warehouse wall, tracksuit, no face. The comments call him the Tracksuit Terror. He has been putting street criminals on the ground in the Dockyards across the month, never killing, always leaving them in a condition that suggests they should reconsider. The post has 400 shares and a local journalist has left a comment asking for the photographer's details.\n\n## Cacophony Savvy 2\n\nThe carpark clip is in its second week of circulation. A figure near the Pyrmont overpass, captured on a dashcam, moving across the asphalt in a way that no person should be able to move. Two Reddit threads. A breakfast-radio segment that played it as a joke. A follow-up piece in the Daily Telegraph that did not play it as a joke. Somebody in the Harbour moved too fast for the cameras and the cameras caught it.\n\n## Cacophony Savvy 3\n\nThe Academy's occult signature has shifted in a way that is not entirely yours.
